Amelia — really appreciate the clear list. Summary below; attaching an initial pricing sheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf) for line-item detail.

High-level:
- Unit & commits: we price reserved commits by "reserved GPU slots" (1 slot ~ full RTX-class GPU with shared vGPU options). Commit terms: 3/6/12 months. 6-month is typical for phased ramps.
- Isolation premium: two components
  1) Platform surcharge: a flat "isolation uplift" equal to +35% of base reserved unit rate (covers single-tenant scheduling, dedicated NVLINK/placement, KV cache isolation).
  2) Compliance add-on: per-account audit-streaming + SIEM connector and extended retention = $3,000/month.
- KMS: integration fee is $7,500 one-time (setup + key rotation policy), then $250/mo key management pass-through for HSM-backed options.
- Throughput SLAs:
  - Standard reserved (no isolation): 95th percentile token latency SLA at committed throughput.
  - Isolation SKU: we guarantee dedicated pool throughput at committed units; for 6-month commits we offer 99th percentile outage credit schedule (details in PDF).
- Discounts: volume discount tiers at 10% / 18% / 25% for 100 / 250 / 500 reserved slots respectively. Additional 3% annual prepay discount for 12-month upfront.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time $25k professional services credit for migration for deals >= 12-month 250-slot commit; for smaller phased deals we can consider a partial credit.

Phased commit proposal (recommended for your use case):
  Phase A (months 1–3): 50 reserved slots, isolation uplift applied, monthly billing.
  Phase B (months 4–6): ramp to 150 reserved slots (60% increase), apply volume discount at 10% once hitting 100.
  Phase C (month 7+): if you convert to a 12-month 250-slot commit, apply 18% discount + $25k onboarding credit.

I'm copying Rafael who manages pricing flexibility on edge cases. Let me know the capacity curve you expect and I will convert this to a formal SOW.

Amelia / Neha — Rafael here, quick clarifications from pricing ops and legal-impact perspective.

1) Credits & discounts: we can accommodate a one-time 5% contract credit applied to the first invoice for deals that convert from a 6-month ramp to a 12-month commit within the first 9 months. For PoC-only customers (3 months) we cannot provide the $25k onboarding credit unless they convert to >=250 slots.

2) KMS fee: we can reduce the monthly KMS pass-through to $212/mo (5% off) if the customer signs a 12-month KMS commitment in contract. That will be surfaced as an addendum to the SOW.

3) SLA language: we'll include explicit credits for p95/p99 breaches under the isolation pool. Typical language: service credit = X% of monthly bill per incident, max Y% per month. We'll provide concrete thresholds in the SOW (I put placeholders in SOW_draft_20260805.docx).

4) Pricing math: to make the phasing clearer, here's an example (numbers illustrative):
   - Phase A (3mo PoC): 50 slots * $10k/slot/mo * isolation uplift 35% = $675k/mo
   - Phase B (3mo ramp): 100 slots * $9.2k/slot/mo (10% volume) * isolation uplift = $12.42M over 3 months
   - Conversion: 250-slot 12mo commit: base $8.2k/slot/mo with 18% discount and onboarding credit eligibility

If you want, Neha and I can produce a month-by-month cashflow table and a redlineable SOW for procurement. Priyom will help with the SOW template and legal pointers.
